title: Multiphoton Microscopic Observation of Vessels in Mouse Liver Tissue
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse.
Prepare sodium pentobarbital (50 mg/kg) in a syringe.
Disinfect the abdominal skin with 75% alcohol.
Pierce the abdomen white line with the needle slightly to the right side of the skin by 3-5 mm at a 45° angle.
Inject the pentobarbital slowly into the abdominal cavity.
Shave around the mouse’s incision site.
Disinfects around the mouse’s incision site three times alternately with 75% alcohol and Chlorhexidine solution.
Check for lack of righting reflex to confirm successful anesthesia.
Prepare 100 μL of 10 mg/mL Rhodamine B isothiocyanate–dextran in a syringe.
Wipe the mouse’s tail with 75% alcohol.
Hold the tail with the left hand and inject the dye with the needle parallel to the vein.
Stop bleeding with a cotton swab after injection.
Soak the mouse’s abdominal fur with gauze wetted with sterile water.
Shave the mouse’s abdomen using a razor, making strokes in the direction of the fur.
Disinfect around the mouse’s incision site three times alternately with 75% alcohol and Chlorhexidine solution.
Wipe a heating pad with 75% alcohol.
Place the mouse on its back in the heating pad to maintain its body temperature at 37 °C.
Install an organ imaging fixture and wipe it with 75% alcohol.
Connect the suction cup (5 mm diameter) to the vacuum pump hose.
Turn on the vacuum pump.
Disinfect around the mouse’s incision site three times alternately with 75% alcohol and Chlorhexidine solution.
Use surgical scissors to cut 2 cm of skin off the lower sternal border of the mouse and expose the liver.
Place the mouse together with the heating pad on the holder base.
Adjust the organ imaging fixture so that the suction cup holds the liver.
Apply a negative pressure of 30-35 kPa for suction so that the liver attaches to the suction cup.
Turn on the multiphoton microscope and select the 60x/1.00 W objective.
Fix the frame and mouse under the objective lens.
Add a drop of normal saline that can cover the entire lens, which is the center of the suction cup, and adjust the objective lens to just touch the normal saline.
Double-click on the computer icon to turn on the laser software and turn on the switch.
Press and hold the power button and shutter for 3 s.
Set the wavelength to 800 nm.
Start the microscope operating software using the computer.
For the Acquisition Setting, set Laser 800.
Click the Fluorescent switch in Image Acquisition Control.
Ensure that the room and equipment lights are switched off.
Use the microscope in a darkened environment to reduce noise levels.
Open the light path shutter on the microscope.
Rotate the fluorescence filter to the fourth gear and pull the two levers of the optical switch.
Looking through the eyepiece, use the coarse and fine focusing quasispirals to adjust the focal length.
Use the X/Y axes to adjust the field of view to find the target area.
Turn off the fluorescent switch on the software.
Switch the fluorescent filter to the second gear (second gear is RXD1).
Push the two levers of the optical switch.
Click Focus ×2 to preview the target area and adjust acquisition settings (image resolution: 1024).
Press Control + C to adjust high voltage, gain, and offset.
Stop the preview by clicking Stop.
Switch to XY mode for two-dimensional scanning.
Save the completed scan.
Select a region, click Depth, and then Preview to set end and start sets.
Scan 3D images and save after completion.
Select a region, click Time, and adjust acquisition settings (Step Size: 1 μm; Slices: 10; Time Scan Number: 40).
Scan different slices and save after completion to obtain moving images.
